title: Finite 8-entry magma-table witness that 854 implies neither 413 nor 1045
intent: Reduce the existential goal `∃ (G : Type) (_ : Magma G), Facts G [854] [413, 1045]` (there is a magma satisfying equation 854 but neither 413 nor 1045) to a single finite 8-entry table: name that table as the witness `e`, take the law and the cancellation property from the greedy-extension accessors `Extension.eq854`/`Extension.aux`, and close the two refutations by evaluating the table with `fromList_eval`.

applicability.goal_shape: ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Magma G), Facts G [e] [f₁, …, fₙ] — an existential over a magma type that must satisfy one equation `e` and refute finitely many others; the witness is a finite partial magma (a literal list of triples `(a,b) ↦ c`) completed to a total magma by a greedy extension.
applicability.use_when: the refutations are determined by a small finite table whose side conditions are decidable (`by decide`), and the law plus the cancellation lemma come from an already-proved extension theorem exposed as accessors, so the witness proof only assembles and evaluates.
applicability.avoid_when: the witness needs infinitely many entries or a side condition `decide` cannot discharge; the law must be re-derived inside the proof rather than taken from an accessor; or the refutation does not reduce to a table evaluation plus one `cases`.

claims.claim: The parent `not_413_1045` is closed from its four direct children: the witness is justified by `⟨⟨_, fromList_ok⟩, rfl⟩` (line 510), the law by `e.eq854` (line 511), six `fromList_eval` table lookups (lines 512, 513, 518, 519, 520, 521), and the two refutations end `cases e.aux this.symm` (line 517) and `cases this` (line 527), with no goal left over.

The main proof is 21 lines (507-527) and combines exactly 4 named lemmas declared in the same file; the longest chain of project lemmas below it, traced by hand, is fromList_eval → Extension.base → exists_extension → exists_greedy_chain, a depth of 4.

consequences: The witness `e` must be proved a valid `Extension`: `⟨⟨_, fromList_ok⟩, rfl⟩` requires `(fromList S).OK`, i.e. all ten side conditions (sorted, eq854, eq8, eq101, eq46155, eq378, no_idem, aux, uniq_fac, mono) of the 8-entry table to be discharged by `decide`, so the burden is shifted onto the decidability of the literal list. The law (854) and the cancellation property are not re-derived for the witness: they are taken from `exists_extension` via `.choose_spec`, so the proof inherits a dependency on the greedy-extension theorem (which itself rests on `exists_greedy_chain` and the ~170-line `next_ok` extension of `PreExtension.OK`, lines 229-397). Failure modes: if `decide` cannot discharge one table side condition, `fromList_ok` fails; if a queried triple is absent from `S`, `fromList_eval`'s `by decide` membership fails; each refutation must reduce to a single falsehood (`e.aux` contradiction for 413, a numeral contradiction for 1045).
